# HAX at Penn State

> HAX at Penn State (https://hax.psu.edu) is Penn State's free, open-source website builder. Penn State students, faculty and staff log in with their Penn State account to create accessible course sites, portfolios, project sites and department sites without writing code. It runs HAXcms from the open-source HAX ecosystem (HAXTheWeb) and is supported by a collaboration of Penn State colleges.

Key facts:

- Cost: free for Penn State users; HAX itself is open source (Apache-2.0) and free for anyone to self-host.
- Who can use hax.psu.edu: anyone with a Penn State account, via https://hax.psu.edu/login.php. Anyone else can try the editor at https://hax.cloud or self-host HAX.
- Typical uses: course materials and open educational resources (OER), student portfolios and resumes, project and department sites.
- Accessibility: published pages must meet Penn State Policy AD69 (Accessibility Standards); HAX is built with accessibility-forward authoring.
- Portability: sites are plain files (HTML + JSON) that can be downloaded and hosted elsewhere, including GitHub Pages and other static hosts.
- Supported by: College of Arts and Architecture, College of Information Sciences and Technology, College of Education, Eberly College of Science and University Libraries, with outside contributors including Buttercups LLC.
- Contact: Bill Rose, Product Owner (bmr1@psu.edu), or hax@psu.edu. Community support on Discord.
- Name: HAX stands for Headless Authoring eXperience. Also referred to as HAXcms, HAXTheWeb or "HAX @ PSU".

## Get started

- [Log in to HAX at Penn State](https://hax.psu.edu/login.php): Penn State WebAccess sign-in; creates or opens your HAX sites.
- [Try HAX without an account](https://hax.cloud): Public demo of the HAX editor.
- [HAX CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@haxtheweb/create): `npm install --global @haxtheweb/create` then `hax start` to build HAX sites locally.
- [Create your first site in 20 seconds (video)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZK3UiOcvag)

## Documentation

- [HAX documentation](https://haxtheweb.org/): Official docs (philosophy, tutorials, component reference).
- [Getting started guide and user blocks](https://haxtheweb.org/welcome)

- [DDD design system](https://haxtheweb.org/ddd)

- [Customer Discovery 101](https://customerdiscovery101.launchbox.psu.edu/): Invent Penn State, Launchbox

- [Issue queue](https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues): Bugs, feature requests and discussion for the whole HAX ecosystem.
- [Source code](https://github.com/haxtheweb): All HAX repositories.
- [Security policy](https://hax.psu.edu/.well-known/security.txt): RFC 9116 security contact.

## Policies

- [Penn State IT Web Services Policy (AD54)](https://policy.psu.edu/policies/ad54)
- [Accessibility Standards (AD69)](https://policies.psu.edu/policies/ad69)
- [Penn State web privacy statement](https://www.psu.edu/web-privacy-statement)

## For AI agents and developers

- [Full homepage content as Markdown](https://hax.psu.edu/llms-full.txt): Everything on hax.psu.edu, including the FAQ, in one file.
- [Agent skills index](https://hax.psu.edu/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): agentskills.io discovery index of curated HAX skills (site building, content authoring, WCAG/UDL/UbD/OER Schema audits, web component development). Each skill's SKILL.md is served alongside it under /.well-known/agent-skills/<name>/. Install them all with `npx skills add haxtheweb/praw --all`.

## Optional

- [Sitemap](https://hax.psu.edu/sitemap.xml)
- [HAX ecosystem overview](https://haxtheweb.org/): HAX is a monorepo of 250+ LitElement web components, the HAXcms file-based CMS, the DDD design system, the HAX CLI and HAX.cloud, built on the pillars Accessible, Extensible, Free and Open, Efficient, Platform Agnostic, Remixable and Sustainable.
